files.receipts.json: Receipt and acknowledgement vectors (ADR-016): fixed issuer and agent keys, the subject pseudonym derivation, two signed receipts that any Ed25519 implementation must reproduce byte for byte, one valid acknowledgement, and the refusals with the error code each must produce. Generated by packages/core/scripts/gen-receipt-vectors.ts; checked on Node and workerd by packages/core/test/receipts-vectors.test.ts.
files.receipts-v2.json: Receipt claims v2 (ADR-017 §3.2): a promise and its outcome for each of the eleven outcomes an inbox records, an acknowledgement naming a pass reference (pas), refused claims with the code a network answers, the outcome table of §3, and every path through the booking and order state machines with the outcome it records (§3.1). Generated by packages/core/scripts/gen-network-vectors.ts; checked by packages/core/test/network-vectors.test.ts.
files.receipts-v6.json: Rules version 6 (ADR-017 Amendment 3): a booking and an order whose promise both sides changed (amended receipts with ref, the new due and end, trm and acc) and the outcome that reads the latest amendment's dates; a refund's promise and each of its outcomes; how a reader on rules 5 takes each receipt (trm and acc ignored, refunds and amendments refused); the claims version 6 still refuses; an acknowledgement of an amendment; the order.refund_refused report and the reasons each report takes; the outcome rows version 6 adds and the amendment limits; every path through the refund machine and every change to a booking or an order. Generated by packages/core/scripts/gen-network-vectors.ts; checked by packages/core/test/network-vectors.test.ts.
files.signatures.json: Signed requests (ADR-017 §2.4, §7.2): sdi-instance/1, sdi-agent/1 with a self-held key and with Web Bot Auth, forwarded signatures (agent_key), each with its signature base, and refusals with their codes. Generated by packages/core/scripts/gen-network-vectors.ts; checked by packages/core/test/network-vectors.test.ts.
files.passes.json: The strings a person holds (key, pass, pass reference, session), ppid, email_mac, secret hashes and email normalisation (ADR-017 §2). Generated by packages/core/scripts/gen-network-vectors.ts; checked by packages/core/test/network-vectors.test.ts.
files.scoring.json: Scores (ADR-017 §5), from the network: every worked example with its scoring_time, the R5 grid, the ageing word cap, hold and release, R32.
files.ordering.json: Order (ADR-017 §6), from the network: rank_shuffle values above 2^53, one snapshot exercising every ORDER BY clause, and cursors.
files.ordering-v7.json: Rules version 7's order (§4.4), from the network: entries at a snapshot time give the order and each one's place, by reach tier, record, the daily shuffle and one place per registrable domain; then, once, on that whole order, every 5th place goes to the next answering newcomer not yet placed (slots). A search narrows this order and never reorders it: pages are cuts of what a filter keeps. Read by packages/core/test/network-vectors.test.ts.
files.profile.json: What a network keeps from a manifest's profile (ADR-017 Amendment 2, A2.5), from the network: each case's profile, read at now, and what is kept. Every field is checked alone and dropped alone; categories are read against vocab/categories.json at vocabulary_version; hours are kept only with a zone the network knows and at least one good window, and closures that ended before now in that zone are dropped. Read by packages/core/test/network-vectors.test.ts.
files.doors-elsewhere.json: What a reader keeps of a manifest's doors_elsewhere, the kinds of request a business takes somewhere else and where: each entry checked alone and dropped alone (an item type of the five, once, and not one the manifest lists in item_types; an https URL on a named host, kept as written). Written by hand; checked on Node and workerd by packages/core/test/doors-elsewhere.test.ts.
files.mcp.json: What an assistant reads from a network's MCP tools (ADR-017 Amendment 2, A2.7), from the network: for each listing as GET /v1/businesses answers it, at now, the card search_businesses and get_business give (the inbox's doors that are https, written as plain URIs and for customers, today's hours in the business's own zone, the standing in words), and one whole answer of each tool. Read by packages/core/test/network-vectors.test.ts.
files.score.json: The agentic score, rules version 2 as amended on 12 October 2026 (§4.13), from the network: for each case a profile and every capability's state (na where it does not apply), and the score, grade, integer numerator n, possible weight and fixes the formula of vocab/score-rules-v2.json gives. Nineteen worked examples (homepage-example is the site's example card; the general ones count book, order or sign up as one capability; venue-jazz-club is scored as a venue; gym-signup-book counts sign up with order, school-enrol with book; five show the amendment of 8 October, and the last two, a shop with the whole order without and with a way to message it, the amendment of 12 October), then 20 cases from a fixed seed. Re-derived by packages/core/test/network-vectors.test.ts with scoreOf and fixesOf.
files.score-v1.json: The same under rules version 1 (vocab/score-rules-v1.json, retired on 7 October 2026): five worked examples, then 20 cases from a fixed seed. Re-derived the same way.
files.door-reports.json: Door reports (protocol §4.15) and the network's own reads of a door (§4.8): calls read at a fixed time against the doors a network lists (400 malformed and 413 too_large for a whole call; each report kept, its time to the minute, or ignored with the first reason that applies), what one report can do by its proof and source, what one read concludes, the door state machine over a door type's reads, and how a source's attempts count. Written by hand; checked on Node and workerd by packages/spec/test/door-reports.test.ts.
files.door-history.json: A door's history (protocol §4.8, ADR-020): what the public sees of one door type at one host on a given day, from the days a network's own reads of the daily set concluded (answered, failed): the dates seen answering, the days checked and answered (a day with one failed check is missed), the share floored from 14 checked days, the last 90 days as a line, since or from…to, and the door types never shown. Written by an implementation of its own, independent of the network's code and of packages/spec's; checked by packages/spec/test/door-history.test.ts and by the network's own tests.
